record.original_question: Conjecture: The derived length of a finite solvable group G does not exceed |Cod(G)| − 1. The Fitting height of G is known to be at most min{|Cod(G)|−1, |Cod(G)|/2+1} (G. Qian, Y. Zeng, J. Group Theory, to appear).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite solvable group. For an irreducible complex character $\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G)$, define its codegree by
$$\mathrm{cod}(\chi) = \frac{|G:\ker\chi|}{\chi(1)},$$
and let
$$\mathrm{Cod}(G) = \{\mathrm{cod}(\chi) : \chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G)\}$$
denote the set of codegrees of $G$. Let $\mathrm{dl}(G)$ denote the derived length of $G$, i.e., the smallest non-negative integer $n$ such that the $n$-th term $G^{(n)}$ of the derived series of $G$ is trivial.

Prove or disprove: for every finite solvable group $G$,
$$\mathrm{dl}(G) \le |\mathrm{Cod}(G)| - 1.$$
artifact.category_tag: character codegrees of finite solvable groups
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Qian and Zeng establishes a bound on the Fitting height of a finite solvable group $G$ in terms of $|\mathrm{Cod}(G)|$, but the stronger conjecture bounding the derived length by $|\mathrm{Cod}(G)|-1$ does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; it remains an active research problem in character codegree theory.

status_evidence.title: Character codegrees in finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on character codegrees including bounds on Fitting height and derived length of solvable groups in terms of |Cod(G)|.
status_evidence.claim: The derived-length bound by |Cod(G)|-1 is discussed as a conjecture in surveys of character codegrees.

status_evidence.title: A dual version of Huppert's ρ-σ conjecture for character codegrees
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relationships between character codegrees and structural invariants of finite (solvable) groups.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds for the derived length of solvable groups in terms of codegree sets remain open in general.
